title: Method handles in place of Method.invoke

blocks.text: A `MethodHandle` is a typed, directly executable reference to a method or a field. Access is checked **once, when the handle is looked up**, not on each call, and `invokeExact` calls it with **its exact type**, no `Object[]` and no boxing, which is what lets the JIT inline it.

A `MethodHandles.Lookup` finds handles: `findVirtual` for an instance method (the handle's first parameter is the receiver), **`findStatic`** for a static one (no receiver), `findGetter` for a field. `MethodHandles.lookup()` sees what its own class may see; for **private members of another class** use **`MethodHandles.privateLookupIn(owner, MethodHandles.lookup())`**.

items: `virtual(owner, name, type)`: a handle for an instance method, of any access level, whose type is exactly the method's type with the receiver first.
`staticMethod(owner, name, type)`: a handle for a static method.
`getter(owner, field, fieldType)`: a handle reading an instance field, of any access level.

cases.says: virtual(Calculator, "multiply", (int,int)int) invoked on a calculator with 6 and 7 is 42, and getter(Calculator, "memory", int) reads 5.
The multiply handle's type is (Calculator,int,int)int, so invokeExact with those exact types returns 42.
staticMethod(Calculator, "add", (int,int)int) takes just the two ints: 3 and 4 give 7.
A getter for the private field secret and a handle for the private method hidden both work.

concepts: A MethodHandle is a typed reference whose access is checked at lookup, and invokeExact calls it with its exact type, without boxing or an Object array.
MethodHandles.privateLookupIn gives a lookup that reaches another class's private members.
